liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Cold Rain And Snow** (3 reviews): Garcia is very energized, repeatedly belting out the 'run me out' verse; Jerry rocks the opening Cold Rain [24][25][32]
- **Scarlet Begonias** (3 reviews): Reviewer says Scarlet cooks, especially the transition jam; Scarlet and Fire rocked the crowd, carrying them into Samson [25][28][33]
- **Althea** (2 reviews): Reviewer singles out Althea among favorites, along with West L.A. Fadeaway, He's Gone and Scarlet; Althea delves into weirdness; reviewer loves it [29][34]
- **They Love Each Other** (1 review): Phil's bass at the start is massive on this recording [27]
- **He's Gone** (1 review): Garcia carries the band through a hard-rocking stretch before Drums, leading into He's Gone [24]
- **Black Peter** (1 review): Reviewer calls Black Peter fitting for the times [29]

## The recordings

- **gd1983-12-27.senn441.andrewf.89483.sbeok.flac16** (recommended): matrix (soundboard mixed with audience mics); 20 songs; 167 min; rated 4.33/5 by 3 [1]. Said about its sound: PA mix problems at the start of the concert, with kick drums too loud [1]
- **gd1983-12-27.176247.nak700.bradt.miller.clugston.flac2496**: audience recording; 20 songs; 169 min [2]
- **gd1983-12-27.164106.senn421.vita.miller.clugston.flac2496**: audience recording; 20 songs; 168 min [4]
- **gd1983-12-27.134872.Nak100CP4.Hill.Keo.Flac1644**: audience recording; 20 songs; 160 min [7]. Said about its sound: Tape pauses between first-set songs, low first-set levels, some hiss, and missing portions of Drums and the encore [7]
- **gd1983-12-27.sbd.walker-scotton.miller.32502.sbeok.flac16**: soundboard; 19 songs; 176 min; rated 3.5/5 by 4 [10]. Said about its sound: Reviewer praises this soundboard upgrade as the one to get [33]
- **gd83-12-27.sbd-patched.hinko.18258.sbeok.shnf**: soundboard; 19 songs; 170 min; rated 3.25/5 by 4 [11]. Said about its sound: Soundboard is flawed: clipping, static in highs and lows, inconsistent stereo mix; reviewer recommends the audience version instead; Soundboard has digital-sounding noise, pops and crackles; reviewer suggests the audience recording instead [25][26]
- **gd83-12-27.fob-senn-silberman.Miller.17961.sbeok.shnf**: source not stated; 19 songs; 171 min; rated 4.29/5 by 7 [14]. Said about its sound: Silberman recording has a PA problem with kick drums in Cold Rain, fixed by song's end; Sound is somewhat hollow compared to a board but has a pleasant in-the-hall quality [27][34]
- **gd83-12-27.aud.barbella.17419.sbeok.shnf**: audience recording; 19 songs; 163 min; rated 4/5 by 4 [18]. Said about its sound: Audience recording has nice presence of Lesh's bass and Brent's keyboard tinkling [24]

## Around the show

- Reviewer says this was the first show where Weir played a Modulus guitar [23]
- Reviewer attended all four nights and won New Year's Eve tickets playing volleyball against Bill Graham and his staff [26]
- Reviewer attended up front with a friend from New York as part of a four-night run [28]
- Show fell on reviewer's 20th birthday; reviewer attended the entire New Year's run [32]
- Reviewer says Lesh's first show with a six-string Modulus bass was 12-26-82 at Oakland Auditorium [23]
- Reviewer thinks this recording's quality beats the soundboard [27]
- Reviewer sees it as a culmination of big runs through the year: spring, summer, fall and December [29]
- Reviewer counts it among their favorite 1980s shows so far [34]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd1983-12-27.senn441.andrewf.89483.sbeok.flac16**: taped by Andrew F.; transferred by Andrew F.; source: Sennheiser MD-441's > patched thru 2 tapedecks > Marantz PMD-340 > Sony UCX-S 90's, Dolby on. Mics on 8-foot stand, just behind the Sbd [1]. Also: Drums/Space made seamless with patches from ShnID-17961; Soundforge used for fades, levels and dropout repair [1]
- **gd1983-12-27.176247.nak700.bradt.miller.clugston.flac2496**: taped by Bill Bradt; transferred by Scott Clugston, Charlie Miller; source: Bill Bradt's Master Audience Cassettes: Nakamichi 700 mics > dbx223 > Sony D5M (TDK MA-90) [2]. Also: A 1:09 patch in the Drums > Space transition comes from the Silberman/Miller Sennheiser 441 source [2]
- **gd1983-12-27.164106.senn421.vita.miller.clugston.flac2496**: taped by Jim Vita; transferred by Scott Clugston, Charlie Miller; source: Jim Vita's Master Audience Cassettes; Sennheiser 421 mics > Sony D5M (Maxell UDXLII-S) [4]. Also: Sennheiser 441 patches supply crowd and start of Cassidy, noodling into He's Gone, and part of Drums [4]
- **gd1983-12-27.134872.Nak100CP4.Hill.Keo.Flac1644**: taped by Steve Hill; transferred by Keo; source: Master Audience Recorded By Steve Hill, Transfer By Keo; Nakamichi CM100/CP4 Shotguns > Unknown Number Of Decks Patched Out Of > Sony TC-D5M, Tapes:Maxell… [7]
- **gd1983-12-27.sbd.walker-scotton.miller.32502.sbeok.flac16**: taped by Joani Walker; transferred by Charlie Miller; source: SBD -> Cassette Master (Nakamichi 550/Maxell XLIIS-90) [10]
- **gd83-12-27.sbd-patched.hinko.18258.sbeok.shnf**: source: SBD > MC > C > DAT > CD > EAC > SHN via Darryl Hinko [11]
- **gd83-12-27.fob-senn-silberman.Miller.17961.sbeok.shnf**: source: (FOB) Senn 441>PCM>Dat recorded by Jeff Silberman encoded by Charlie Miller [14]
- **gd83-12-27.aud.barbella.17419.sbeok.shnf**: source: Aud>?>CD>EAC>SHN via Steve Barbella [18]

claims.text: Reviewer says this was the first show where Weir played a Modulus guitar
Reviewer says Lesh's first show with a six-string Modulus bass was 12-26-82 at Oakland Auditorium
Garcia is very energized, repeatedly belting out the 'run me out' verse
Garcia carries the band through a hard-rocking stretch before Drums, leading into He's Gone
Audience recording has nice presence of Lesh's bass and Brent's keyboard tinkling
Reviewer says Scarlet cooks, especially the transition jam
Jerry rocks the opening Cold Rain
Soundboard is flawed: clipping, static in highs and lows, inconsistent stereo mix; reviewer recommends the audience version instead
Soundboard has digital-sounding noise, pops and crackles; reviewer suggests the audience recording instead
Reviewer attended all four nights and won New Year's Eve tickets playing volleyball against Bill Graham and his staff
Silberman recording has a PA problem with kick drums in Cold Rain, fixed by song's end
Phil's bass at the start is massive on this recording
Reviewer thinks this recording's quality beats the soundboard
Reviewer attended up front with a friend from New York as part of a four-night run
Scarlet and Fire rocked the crowd, carrying them into Samson
Reviewer calls Black Peter fitting for the times
Reviewer singles out Althea among favorites, along with West L.A. Fadeaway, He's Gone and Scarlet
Reviewer sees it as a culmination of big runs through the year: spring, summer, fall and December
Show fell on reviewer's 20th birthday; reviewer attended the entire New Year's run
Reviewer's all-time favorite song, which made the opener special on their birthday
Scarlet>Fire is long, intricate and exploratory; reviewer ranks it among the best heard
The transition jam, dubbed 'Jello Jam', features Weir's heavy whammy bar work and added effects
Reviewer praises this soundboard upgrade as the one to get
Sound is somewhat hollow compared to a board but has a pleasant in-the-hall quality
Althea delves into weirdness; reviewer loves it
Reviewer counts it among their favorite 1980s shows so far
New transfer and upgrade of the ShnID-17419 recording, using a Sennheiser 441 source
Drums/Space made seamless with patches from ShnID-17961; Soundforge used for fades, levels and dropout repair
PA mix problems at the start of the concert, with kick drums too loud
Source is Nak 700 master cassettes from Bill Bradt and Kathy Weir Bradt, transferred by Charlie Miller
A 1:09 patch in the Drums > Space transition comes from the Silberman/Miller Sennheiser 441 source
Source is Sennheiser 421 master cassettes from Jim Vita, transferred by Charlie Miller
Sennheiser 441 patches supply crowd and start of Cassidy, noodling into He's Gone, and part of Drums
Tape pauses between first-set songs, low first-set levels, some hiss, and missing portions of Drums and the encore
Source recorded on Nak 100 by Steve, shared for this show
